Subject: Query on July invoice — token totals look off

Hi Karthik,

We've been reviewing our July invoice (attached) and the overall token count looks much higher than expected — the invoice shows ~3.2M tokens for July but our internal logs indicate closer to ~1.6M. There are two obvious spikes on Jul 12 and Jul 19 where usage jumped by an order of magnitude for a few hours.

Attached is our export from the integration (redwood-usage-log-2026-07.csv) and the invoice (invoice_July2026.pdf). Can you help explain:
- How token attribution is calculated for retried/duplicated requests (we had a retry flood on Jul 19 after a downstream outage).
- Whether prefix caching or KV cache can cause double-counting in the exported logs vs your billing meter.
- How VAT was applied — we expected reverse-charge (no VAT) but the invoice shows VAT added for July.

We need a short summary and corrective action plan (including any credits) by end of week as our finance team needs to close the month.

Thanks,
Tanya Singh
Head of Integrations — BrightEdge Analytics

Hi Tanya / BrightEdge billing — thanks for the detailed export and the note, and thank you Laura and Marcus for the quick turnaround. Summary of findings and actions: 

1) Root cause: Marcus confirmed that 452,918 of the billed requests during the Jul 19 window were duplicates that should not have been billed. Those were client-side replays that bypassed any client-side de-duplication. Our meter counted tokens per received request, which is consistent with the contract, but we agree this was an operational issue tied to the replay and we will make an exception credit for the duplicated volume.

2) Credit: We will apply a pro-rated credit for 452,918 requests = approx. 512,000 tokens (after accounting for average tokenization), equivalent to $1,280.00. This credit will be applied to your August account balance and reflected in a corrected July invoice.

3) VAT correction: Finance confirmed BrightEdge's VAT ID (on file) and that reverse-charge should have applied. Laura will issue a corrected invoice removing VAT for July and re-issue with the same invoice number + "corrected" suffix. Expect corrected invoice and credit note within 48 hours.

4) Preventative steps: engineering will add a short-term metering heuristic to flag sudden replay spikes and proactively mark them for manual review. We'll follow up with a longer-term option to offer de-duplication as a configurable feature.

Next deliverables (by Mon 24 Aug EOD):
- Corrected invoice (Laura)
- Credit note applied to account (finance ledger)
- Token breakdown report with request IDs used for reconciliation (Marcus) — shared via the secure Drive link below.
